all_objections.title: Complexity in ACE and Research interaction
all_objections.detail: The proposal allows Agent #6 to either consume ACE outputs or perform self-crawls, introducing complexity in the codebase. This dual-path approach could lead to maintenance challenges and inconsistencies in data handling, as seen in §1 of the Agent #6 specification.

all_objections.title: Lack of clear rubric versioning
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not adequately address how rubric versioning will be managed, particularly in G8-Q2. Without a clear versioning policy, historical audit scores may become incomparable, leading to potential misinterpretations of product quality over time.

all_objections.title: Insufficient budget cap enforcement
all_objections.detail: The proposal suggests multiple locations for enforcing budget caps (G6-Q4), but lacks a unified approach. This could lead to inconsistent enforcement and potential overspending, especially if different agents or components enforce caps independently.

all_objections.title: Lack of rollback
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case of failures or errors, which could lead to significant disruptions in the system.

all_objections.title: Insufficient testing
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient information about the testing strategy and protocols, which could lead to undetected bugs and errors.

all_objections.title: Over-reliance on third-party tools
all_objections.detail: The proposal relies heavily on third-party tools and services, which could lead to vendor lock-in and make it difficult to switch to alternative solutions if needed.

all_objections.title: Overly complex agent interactions
all_objections.detail: The proposal introduces complex interactions between multiple agents, such as Agent #6 consuming outputs from Agent #21. This complexity can lead to difficulties in debugging and maintaining the system. For example, §15.2 describes the MessageBus with 65 topic constants, which adds significant overhead in managing inter-agent communications.

all_objections.title: Lack of clear budget enforcement
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not clearly specify where budget caps should be enforced. For instance, §7.3 mentions a per-product `researchBudgetCap`, but it is unclear whether this should be enforced inside Agent #6, in Orchestra `dispatchWithFallback`, or elsewhere. This ambiguity can lead to budget overruns and unpredictable costs.

all_objections.title: Inadequate handling of auth-gated content
all_objections.detail: The proposal suggests blocking on any auth-required signal, which can be overly conservative and hinder the system's ability to process partially authenticated content. This can lead to incomplete or inaccurate assessments, as described in §7.4. A more nuanced approach is needed to handle mixed authentication scenarios.

all_objections.title: Limited flexibility in design spec versioning
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear mechanism for handling design spec versioning. For example, §G7-Q5 discusses whether the design spec should be immutable or mutable within a run window. This lack of flexibility can limit the ability to iterate on designs and incorporate operator feedback effectively.

all_objections.title: Complex Dependency Management
all_objections.detail: The proposal introduces complex dependencies between agents, particularly with Agent #6 Research and Agent #21 ACE Conductor. This could lead to delays and complications in the development and deployment process.

all_objections.title: Unclear Authority Boundaries
all_objections.detail: The authority levels and operational boundaries for agents like Agent #6 Research and Agent #8 Quality Audit are not clearly defined, which could lead to confusion and potential security risks.

all_objections.title: Potential for Over-Engineering
all_objections.detail: The proposal suggests multiple layers of checks, audits, and configurable options that may lead to over-engineering, making the system more complex and harder to maintain.

all_objections.title: Executor naming ambiguity
all_objections.detail: §15.5 mentions `executorKey` in audit logs, but the `ExecutorRecord` interface uses `key` as the unique identifier. This inconsistency could lead to confusion and errors in implementation and debugging.

all_objections.title: Agent #6 crawl fallback risk
all_objections.detail: G6-Q1's soft dependency on ACE for Agent #6 introduces a risk of inconsistent crawl results if ACE is unavailable, potentially skewing research findings and downstream processes. The fallback mechanism might not perfectly replicate ACE's crawl behavior.

all_objections.title: Agent #8 rubric versioning
all_objections.detail: G8-Q2's rubric versioning policy lacks clarity on how major version bumps affect existing governance records. If a major version bump invalidates previous scores, there should be a clear migration path or deprecation strategy for historical data.

all_objections.title: Agent #10 webhook vendor lock-in
all_objections.detail: G10-Q1's focus on specific webhook vendors (Zendesk, Intercom, Help Scout) could lead to vendor lock-in and limit the system's adaptability to new or less common platforms. A more generic webhook receiver might be a more flexible solution.

all_objections.title: Partial crawl handling risks
all_objections.detail: G6-Q3's partial ACE artifact acceptance could lead to incomplete research briefs. Accepting partial inputs without supplementation risks propagating low-confidence findings downstream to Design and Build agents, compromising product quality.

all_objections.title: Rubric versioning ambiguity
all_objections.detail: G8-Q2 lacks immutable snapshotting for audit scores. Without embedding rubric content in governance_record_entry, historical score comparability breaks when rubrics evolve, violating audit trail integrity and Locked Rule 1.

all_objections.title: Executor dependency deadlock
all_objections.detail: G7-Q1 hard-gates Design Phase 2 on v0 Probation status. If v0 faces delays, this blocks symbiotic-loop functionality across dependent agents like Monitor and GTM, creating system-wide bottlenecks.

all_objections.title: Cross-tenant data exposure
all_objections.detail: G11-Q5's cross-tenant aggregation risks confidential data leakage. Without strict tenant isolation in Strategic Intelligence, sensitive operator insights could surface in FlowAI's global analysis, violating commercial confidentiality.

all_objections.title: ACE fallback duplicates crawl paths
all_objections.detail: In G6-Q1, the soft-dependency design lets Agent #6 both consume `21.crawl.completed.v1` and self-crawl on fallback. That creates two crawl implementations to keep semantically aligned, increasing drift risk between the ACE artifact and Research’s own crawler behavior. The spec also says Agent #6 is the pipeline entry, so blocking on an upstream soft dependency is a recurring source of non-determinism.

all_objections.title: Partial-data policy is under-specified
all_objections.detail: G6-Q3 admits partial ACE output but does not define minimum coverage, normalization rules, or how missing-page bias affects the brief. Accepting 3/8 pages can systematically over-weight the pages ACE happened to find, especially on sites with auth walls or dynamic navigation. The proposal lacks a provenance model for which pages were omitted and why, so downstream consumers may misread low-confidence output as complete coverage.

all_objections.title: Budget enforcement split across layers
all_objections.detail: G6-Q4 leaves ambiguity between `dispatchWithFallback`, Agent #6 self-checks, and Agent #23 Cost Governor. If multiple layers enforce the same cap, they can race and produce double-failures or inconsistent error reasons; if only one layer does, the others become stale bypass surfaces. The spec does not define a single authoritative ledger read/write path or whether budget consumption is reserved atomically before dispatch.

all_objections.title: Auth-block rule can mask useful coverage
all_objections.detail: G6-Q5’s conservative blocking on any auth-required signal risks turning a site with one logged-in support page into a total no-go, even when all public product and pricing pages are available. That means the system may refuse to classify products where the most valuable public evidence is already sufficient, reducing coverage and increasing operator workload. The proposal does not separate hard security boundaries from ordinary gated content, so it can over-trigger on benign authenticated help docs.

all_objections.title: Audit rubric immutability harms iteration
all_objections.detail: G8-Q2 and G8-Q1 together risk freezing early rubric mistakes into the governance pipeline. If rubrics are pinned forever, a scoring defect discovered after launch forces a parallel versioning regime with broken comparability or a permanent fork of historical audits. The spec does not define a migration policy for already-scored products when rubric semantics are corrected, which makes regressions hard to repair cleanly.

all_objections.title: Tight Coupling Between Agents
all_objections.detail: The proposal introduces a complex inter-agent dependency graph (§15.2). For example, Agent #6 Research depends on Agent #21 ACE Conductor, and Agent #8 Quality Audit depends on both Agent #6 and Agent #7. This tight coupling may lead to cascading failures and make it challenging to maintain or update individual agents without affecting others.

all_objections.title: Lack of Clear Error Handling
all_objections.detail: The proposal lacks a clear error handling mechanism (§10). For instance, Agent #6 Research has an `escalationPolicy` (§7.4) that is not fully specified, and Agent #8 Quality Audit's handling of partial ACE artifacts (§G8-Q3) is not clearly defined. This ambiguity may result in unhandled errors or inconsistent behavior.

all_objections.title: Insufficient Configuration Options
all_objections.detail: Some configuration options, such as the 95/95 threshold for Quality Audit (§G8-Q3), are not operator-configurable. This lack of flexibility may limit the proposal's adaptability to different operator needs or environments.

all_objections.title: Agent #21 pending wire-in
all_objections.detail: §15.1 Roster marks Agent #21 DORMANT with 'engineering wire-in pending'; this directly affects AGENT_06_Research.md §1 soft dependency where Research consumes 21.crawl.completed.v1 or falls back to self-crawl, creating duplicate crawl paths with no rollback.

all_objections.title: EXECUTOR_REGISTRY validator conflict
all_objections.detail: §15.5 validateExecutors() cross-links to AGENT_REGISTRY while §25 Locked Rule 2 mandates exactly 26 IDs via validateRosterPartition(); adding split-charter executors like self-renewal-executor risks ID collision or partition violation at BaseAgent.js load time.

all_objections.title: Inline rubric centralization risk
all_objections.detail: G6-Q2 and G8-Q1 retain Five-Layer rubric as single prompt prefix in src/lib/operationsEngine.js without per-Layer ratification files; this contradicts Locked Rule 5 multi-AI peer review and §10 5-dimension scoring engine owned by Agent #8.

all_objections.title: Cross-tenant data isolation breach
all_objections.detail: Agent #12 Portfolio Risk's §10 G12-Q1 proposes multi-tenant aggregation options without specifying encryption or data isolation mechanisms. The 'cross-tenant anonymization' option could leak competitive intelligence between operators sharing a FlowAI deployment.

all_objections.title: Unvalidated legal automation risk
all_objections.detail: Agent #14 Public Policy §10 G14-Q4 proposes auto-updating operator terms-of-use pages based on LLM regulatory assessments. This creates liability exposure as LLM-generated legal text modifications lack attorney-client privilege and could introduce non-compliant language.

all_objections.title: Benchmark gaming vulnerability
all_objections.detail: Agent #15 Benchmarking's 30-invocation minimum (§15.1 CA-9-B) is too low for statistical significance. Malicious Orchestra candidates could game the system by performing well on initial invocations then degrading, especially with the single-judge LLM evaluation proposed in G15-Q3.

all_objections.title: DMCA automation without safeguards
all_objections.detail: Agent #13 Self-Protection Phase 2 proposes supervised DMCA letter filing (§10.2) but lacks false-positive mitigation. Automated DMCA takedowns based on watermark detection could target legitimate fair-use cases, exposing operators to counter-claims and liability.

all_objections.title: Ambiguity in cross-tenant aggregation
all_objections.detail: In §1 of the Portfolio Risk agent, the scope is marked as `flowai-only`, but §22 implies multi-tenant generality. This ambiguity could lead to inconsistent data handling and privacy issues if not clarified.

all_objections.title: Lack of auto-remediation clarity
all_objections.detail: In G12-Q4, the proposal lacks clarity on the conditions under which auto-remediation should occur. Without clear guidelines, there is a risk of either over-triggering or missing critical remediation opportunities.

all_objections.title: Inadequate legal oversight for DMCA
all_objections.detail: In G13-Q2, the proposal suggests options that might not involve legal counsel in DMCA processes. This could expose operators to legal risks if DMCA notices are improperly handled.

all_objections.title: Lack of Rollback
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case of errors or unintended consequences, which could lead to significant disruptions to the system. Specifically, §15.1 does not mention any rollback procedures for the 26-agent roster.

all_objections.title: Insufficient Testing
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient information about the testing procedures for the new agents, which could lead to errors or bugs in the system. For example, §10 of AGENT #12 Portfolio Risk does not mention any specific testing protocols.

all_objections.title: Overreliance on LLMs
all_objections.detail: The proposal relies heavily on Large Language Models (LLMs) for various tasks, which could lead to biases or errors in the system. For instance, §15.3 mentions the use of LLMs for benchmarking, but does not provide any information about how to mitigate potential biases.

all_objections.title: Ambiguity in cross-tenant aggregation
all_objections.detail: The proposal for Agent #12 does not clearly define the scope of cross-tenant aggregation. This could lead to confusion and potential misuse of data across tenants.

all_objections.title: Lack of clear deprecation criteria
all_objections.detail: The deprecation window for Agent #17 is set to 60 days, but this may be too conservative or too aggressive depending on the context. There is no adaptive mechanism proposed.

all_objections.title: Inconsistent mode classification
all_objections.detail: The mode classification for Agent #17 is inconsistent between the registry and the blueprint. This inconsistency could lead to operational confusion and errors.

all_objections.title: Scope Ambiguity
all_objections.detail: The proposal for Agent #12 lacks clarity on whether the aggregation is single-tenant or multi-tenant, which could lead to confusion and misconfiguration (§10 G12-Q1).

all_objections.title: Risk Tiering
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not adequately address how different risk tiers for vendors will be managed, potentially leading to oversights in critical vendor dependencies (§10 G12-Q2).

all_objections.title: Threshold Definitions
all_objections.detail: The definitions for P0, P1, and P2 thresholds are not clearly specified, which could result in inconsistent handling of portfolio risks (§10 G12-Q3).

all_objections.title: Agent 12 scope unclear
all_objections.detail: G12-Q1 asks about cross-tenant aggregation, but the implications for data privacy and security are not fully explored.  The proposal doesn't address how tenant data is isolated and protected, especially in multi-tenant scenarios.

all_objections.title: Agent 13 cost risk
all_objections.detail: G13-Q1 discusses Cloudflare Bot Management, but the cost implications are significant and potentially unsustainable, especially if adopted across all products. The proposal lacks a detailed cost-benefit analysis and a plan for managing these expenses.

all_objections.title: Agent 14 legal liability
all_objections.detail: G14-Q1 considers legal counsel review, but the proposal doesn't fully address the legal risks associated with providing regulatory assessments, even if advisory. The disclaimer of liability may not be sufficient to protect FlowAI from legal challenges.

all_objections.title: Agent 15 fixture set bias
all_objections.detail: G15-Q1 discusses fixture set ownership, but the potential for bias in the fixture sets is not adequately addressed. If W3 drafts the fixture sets, there is a risk that they will be biased towards certain capabilities or vendors, skewing the benchmarking results.

all_objections.title: Agent #13 Cloudflare cost risk
all_objections.detail: Agent #13's Phase 2 Cloudflare dependency (§G13-Q1) introduces $200+/month costs without clear ROI analysis. This violates Locked Rule 8's cost-aware budgeting and could lead to operator opt-outs, reducing system security.

all_objections.title: Portfolio Risk topic sprawl
all_objections.detail: G12-Q5's proposed 7 topics conflict with MessageSchema.js's 65-topic limit. Uncontrolled topic proliferation risks message bus congestion and violates §15.2's 'curated industry-tracker' design principle.

all_objections.title: Benchmark statistical weakness
all_objections.detail: CA-9-B's 30-invocation minimum (G15-Q5) provides insufficient statistical power for capability comparisons. At 95% confidence, this yields ±18% margin of error - worse than Amazon Mechanical Turk's rejected 2015 HIT standards.

all_objections.title: Legal liability blindspot
all_objections.detail: Agent #14's English-only Phase 1 (G14-Q3) creates regulatory blindspots - e.g. missing French CNIL guidance. This mirrors 2021 Clearview AI's $20M GDPR fine from lacking multilingual compliance.

all_objections.title: Cross-tenant scope is underspecified
all_objections.detail: §10 G12-Q1 leaves `flowAiOnly: true` in tension with the artifact's multi-tenant language and does not define whether aggregation happens at deployment, tenant, or industry level. That matters because Portfolio Risk can easily become a covert cross-tenant intelligence channel if the wrong mode is chosen, especially once it ingests vendor concentration and fire signals.

all_objections.title: P0 semantics are unstable
all_objections.detail: §10 G12-Q3 proposes several incompatible definitions of P0/P1/P2, but the proposal never anchors them to a measurable operational objective like user harm, outage duration, or remediation SLA. Without one canonical thresholding scheme, the same incident could oscillate between classes depending on who labels it, breaking alert routing and trend analysis.

all_objections.title: Auto-handoff can create cascades
all_objections.detail: §10 G12-Q4 asks whether Portfolio Risk should hand off to Self-Renewal Executor, but there is no explicit debounce, deduplication, or rollback rule for repeated fires. If a vendor outage causes a flood of P0s, an eager auto-handoff loop could trigger parallel remediation attempts and amplify instability rather than contain it.

all_objections.title: Topic reconciliation is inconsistent
all_objections.detail: §10 G12-Q5 acknowledges a mismatch between `_registry.ts` topics and the blueprint's `12.portfolio_risk.v1` / `12.product_alert.v1`, yet none of the listed options addresses namespace collision risk or backward compatibility for consumers. Adding topics ad hoc without a migration plan could strand downstream listeners or produce duplicate alerts.

all_objections.title: Lack of Rollback Mechanism
all_objections.detail: The proposal under §15.5 for EXECUTOR_REGISTRY lacks a clear rollback mechanism in case an executor is incorrectly configured or causes issues. This could lead to operational disruptions.

all_objections.title: Ambiguity in Cross-Tenant Aggregation
all_objections.detail: The scope of Portfolio Risk aggregation is unclear (§G12-Q1). If not properly isolated, this could lead to cross-tenant data leakage or incorrect risk assessments.

all_objections.title: Insufficient Error Handling in Auto-Handoff
all_objections.detail: The auto-handoff mechanism for P0 fires (§G12-Q4) lacks detailed error handling. If Self-Renewal Executor fails to mitigate, the issue could escalate without operator intervention.

all_objections.title: Agent #12 authority mismatch
all_objections.detail: §1 Build-authority is recommend_only yet G12-Q4 auto-remediation hand-off options assume direct dispatch to Self-Renewal Executor; this violates the dual-authority + requires_human_gate invariant in canonical §15.5 and CA-9-Q4=(b) for any auto_write_internal path.

all_objections.title: Mode declaration conflict
all_objections.detail: G17-Q1 shows _registry.ts declares cross-step for Agent #17 while blueprint claims always-on; this directly contradicts Locked Rule 2 roster partition and §15.1 canonical table that fixes mode per agent ID without reconciliation mechanism.

all_objections.title: Unbounded cost and dependency risk
all_objections.detail: G13-Q1 and G15-Q2 introduce Cloudflare ($200+/mo) plus $1,125/mo benchmark baseline with no rollback or cap enforcement in §22 product-agnostic rule or §25 Locked Rule 8; dormant status in §1 leaves weekly jobs unwired per canonical §15.2.

all_objections.title: Ops Runner role ambiguity creates deadlock
all_objections.detail: §22-§25 all declare DORMANT status BLOCKED on §27 OQ-2 disposition, but §27 is not included in the bundle. This creates a circular dependency where 4 agents cannot progress without external resolution, risking permanent dormancy.

all_objections.title: Agent #26 dual-authority precedent risk
all_objections.detail: §26 introduces the first primary-agent with dual-authority `[recommend_only, auto_write_internal, requires_human_gate]` per G26-Q2. This breaks the established pattern where elevated authority lives in EXECUTOR_REGISTRY, potentially undermining the security model.

all_objections.title: Cost Governor mode mismatch
all_objections.detail: Agent #23 §1 declares `step-owner` mode in _registry.ts but §10 G23-Q2 recommends `cross-step` since cost is cross-cutting. This fundamental mode disagreement suggests the charter is architecturally misaligned.

all_objections.title: Environmental Impact carbon factors unverified
all_objections.detail: Agent #20 G20-Q1 proposes using static lookup tables or third-party APIs for carbon emission factors, but provides no validation mechanism to ensure these factors remain accurate or legally compliant across jurisdictions.

all_objections.title: Inconsistent Topic Naming
all_objections.detail: In §10 of Agent #18, there is inconsistency in topic naming between `_registry.ts` and the blueprint. This could lead to confusion and errors in message handling if not reconciled properly.

all_objections.title: Dual-Authority Risk
all_objections.detail: Agent #26 introduces a dual-authority model at the primary-agent layer, which is a significant architectural change. This could lead to increased complexity and potential security risks if not managed carefully.

all_objections.title: Escalation Policy Ambiguity
all_objections.detail: The escalation policy for Agent #22 is vague, stating 'escalate to #1 on any side effect attempt.' This lacks specificity and could lead to inconsistent handling of issues.

all_objections.title: Lack of Rollback
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case of failures or errors, which could lead to system instability and data loss. Specifically, §15.1 Roster table does not mention any rollback mechanism for Agent #3 Self-Renewal.

all_objections.title: Insufficient Error Handling
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient error handling mechanisms, which could lead to system crashes or unexpected behavior. For example, §15.2 Interaction model does not specify how errors will be handled in the MessageBus pub/sub system.

all_objections.title: Inadequate Security Measures
all_objections.detail: The proposal does not provide adequate security measures to prevent unauthorized access or data breaches. Specifically, §15.3 OrchestratorHub ↔ Orchestra relationship does not mention any security protocols for protecting sensitive data.

all_objections.title: Ambiguous authority roles
all_objections.detail: The proposal for Agent #26 introduces dual-authority (recommend_only, auto_write_internal, requires_human_gate) which is complex and may lead to confusion in implementation. This is particularly concerning given the security-critical nature of auto-admission tasks.

all_objections.title: Potential escalation policy gaps
all_objections.detail: The escalation policy for Agent #22 is described as 'escalate to #1 on any side effect attempt,' which is vague. There needs to be a clear definition of what constitutes a 'side effect attempt' to avoid misinterpretation.

all_objections.title: Inconsistent topic naming
all_objections.detail: There are discrepancies in topic naming conventions across different agents. For example, Agent #18 has multiple topic names that need reconciliation. This inconsistency can lead to integration issues and confusion.

all_objections.title: Lack of clear dependency management
all_objections.detail: Several agents depend on the successful implementation and shipping of other agents or components. For instance, Agent #20 depends on the Orchestra cost-ledger being live. This creates a complex web of dependencies that could delay the entire project if one component fails.

all_objections.title: Dual-authority risk
all_objections.detail: Agent #26 is the first primary agent with dual-authority, which could lead to complex interactions and potential security risks if not carefully managed.

all_objections.title: Complexity in topic management
all_objections.detail: The proposal introduces multiple new topics for Agent #18, which could lead to confusion and increased maintenance overhead.

all_objections.title: Unclear escalation policy
all_objections.detail: The escalation policy for Agent #22 is vague and may not provide sufficient guidance for handling side effects.

all_objections.title: Executor naming inconsistency
all_objections.detail: §15.5 uses `key` for executor identifiers, but the cross-link with §14 GovernanceAuditLog uses `executorKey`. This inconsistency could lead to confusion and errors when querying or analyzing audit logs.

all_objections.title: Agent #26 dual authority risk
all_objections.detail: Agent #26's dual authority (`auto_write_internal` and `requires_human_gate`) at the primary agent layer is a significant departure from the established pattern. While CA-9-Q4=(b) ratified it, the potential for unintended consequences and security vulnerabilities warrants extreme caution. The proposal lacks a clear justification for why the Executor pattern wasn't used instead.

all_objections.title: Ops Runner role overlap
all_objections.detail: The proposed roles for Ops Runners #22-#25 seem to have overlapping responsibilities. For example, both #24 (Audit Trail Integrity Conductor) and #23 (Cost Governor) could potentially trigger alerts that require workflow orchestration, potentially duplicating effort and creating conflicts.

all_objections.title: Lack of rollback strategy
all_objections.detail: The proposal lacks a clear rollback strategy for changes made by agents with `auto_write_internal` authority, particularly Agent #26. If an agent makes an incorrect or malicious change to the system, there needs to be a well-defined process for reverting to a previous state.

all_objections.title: Agent #26 atomic write risk
all_objections.detail: The file-lock + atomic-rename pattern for CANONICAL_HISTORY writes in §G26-Q4 fails to address distributed system concurrency. Under high load, multiple admission processes could race the lock, potentially corrupting Orchestra membership records. This violates Locked Rule 1 (anti-drift) and lacks transactional guarantees.

all_objections.title: Agent #19 CVE enforcement gap
all_objections.detail: The hybrid critical-CVE SLA enforcement mechanism in §G19-Q3 creates alerting gaps during Inngest event processing delays. If synchronous emits fail and backstop jobs queue behind other tasks, critical vulnerabilities may breach the 60s SLA without alert escalation paths. The monitor agent (#10) lacks compensating controls for this failure mode.

all_objections.title: Agent #23 mode conflict
all_objections.detail: §G23-Q2 proposes changing Agent #23 to cross-step mode while the registry declares step-owner. This violates §15.2 OrchestratorHub's routing invariants and risks step-owner collisions. The validator lacks mode-change safeguards, potentially breaking AutoRunner's step ownership resolution.

all_objections.title: Topic proliferation risk
all_objections.detail: §G18-Q1's multiple topic options violate MessageSchema cardinality principles from §15.2. Adding three distinct topics for Agent #18 without payload consolidation risks message bus congestion and consumer agent complexity spikes, contradicting the product-agnostic rule's simplicity mandate.

all_objections.title: Agent #26 dual-authority risk
all_objections.detail: Agent #26 is the first primary agent with dual-authority charter, which may introduce architectural risks (§15.1, §26). The precedent set by CA-9-Q4=(b) may not be thoroughly vetted for all primary agents.

all_objections.title: Ops Runner roles unclear
all_objections.detail: The roles for Ops Runner Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Epsilon are TBD or pending disposition (§22, §23, §24, §25). This uncertainty may lead to inconsistent or inefficient allocation of responsibilities.

all_objections.title: Inconsistent topic naming
all_objections.detail: There are discrepancies in topic naming conventions across agents (e.g., Agent #18 produces `18.plan.update.v1` but blueprint suggests additional topics). This inconsistency may cause confusion or errors in inter-agent communication (§10, G18-Q1).

all_objections.title: Reserved Ops Runner charters lack roles
all_objections.detail: §15.1 Roster and Locked Rule 2 declare exactly 26 agents with #22-#25 as DORMANT step-owners; G22-Q1/G24-Q1/G25-Q1 list only plausible roles with no canonical assignment, so validateRosterPartition() and OrchestratorHub.invokeStepOwner will fail on any dispatch attempt.

all_objections.title: Dual-authority on primary #26
all_objections.detail: G26-Q2 and §15.5 allow Agent #26 primary charter to carry [recommend_only, auto_write_internal, requires_human_gate] directly; this bypasses the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY sibling namespace and the 25-ID partition invariant enforced by BaseAgent.js and validateExecutors().

all_objections.title: Topic naming drift across agents
all_objections.detail: G18-Q1, G20-Q4 and §15.2 show _registry.ts emitting only 18.plan.update.v1 / 20.impact.assessment.v1 while blueprints add extra topics, expanding the 65-topic set without any reconciliation or schema-migration mechanism in MessageBus or MessageSchema.js.
